reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' and the cited text supports it: Section 4(a) gives the Customer (AP) a for-any-reason termination right on ninety (90) days' written notice after the Initial Term, which sits squarely inside the fallback's 60–90 day window; no redline or comment is expected for a compliant finding, and none was proposed.

The Initial Term is exactly one (1) year, so the detection trigger for 'absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months' is not met; auto-renewal in 1-year increments with a 90-day exit right is not a multi-year lock-in, so the walk-away band is not reached.

Vendor-side exit is on 90 days' notice, i.e. not 'fewer than 90 days', so the walk-away threshold for Vendor convenience termination is not triggered. The fact that Kubient's right is not confined to term-end is correctly treated as a sub-element short of preferred wording and noted in the rationale rather than flagged, and the right is symmetric rather than one-sided against us.

The economics are read fairly: Kubient's entitlement to fees 'generated during the termination period' is effectively the ~3 months of the notice period, consistent with the fallback's cap of no more than 3 months' fees, and it applies to either terminating party.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing false negative — the right is expressed as 'Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice' rather than naming the Customer — so it does not undercut the compliant classification.
Absence of a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is correctly explained as inapplicable to a revenue-share structure where Kubient remits to AP rather than AP prepaying fees; this is noted, not over-flagged.
